claims.statement: After Allen's death, Lord Barrington wore Allen's silk hat, which J. W. Gillespie had fitted him out with.
claims.excerpt: who originally fitted Barrington out with this personal effect of Allen's

claims.statement: Tillie Hartgrove, Allen's housekeeper, claimed the silk hat as a keepsake of the old pugilist.
claims.excerpt: Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove, Tom Allen's housekeeper, who claimed it as a keepsake of the old pugilist

claims.statement: Hartgrove and J. W. Gillespie went to Clayton and failed to get the hat from Barrington, who denied having it.
claims.excerpt: Last week Mrs. Hartgrove, accompanied by J. W. Gillespie, went to Clayton and vainly endeavored to induce Barrington to give up the hat.

claims.statement: Hartgrove and Gillespie left Clayton threatening to replevin (sue to recover) the hat.
claims.excerpt: Mrs. Hartgrove and Gillespie finally left, threatening to replevin the tile.

claims.statement: Barrington returned the disputed hat by messenger boy with a note reading 'From Barington'.
claims.excerpt: Friday afternoon a messenger boy returned the disputed property with a simple note

claims.statement: Paddy Nalty, who had worked for Allen for six years, pronounced the hat the genuine Tom Allen relic.
claims.excerpt: The tile is pronounced the genuine Tom Allen relic by Paddy Nalty, who had worked for Allen for six years

claims.statement: The hat was put on display for Allen's friends, along with the silver cup he won in 1878.
claims.excerpt: It is now exposed for the veneration of all friends of the dead pugilist, along with the silver cup

claims.statement: Tom Allen won a silver cup with the English heavyweight championship in 1878.
claims.excerpt: the silver cup that Allen won with the heavy-weight championship of England in 1878

notes: All hints checked; the first hint is split into death, worn-by and housekeeper claims. Barrington's arrest for the McCann murder is not about Allen and is not recorded.
